newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goodman says in no hurry for purchase.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goodman says in no hurry for purchase.

text.p: Australian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Wednesday it would decide within the next 12 months to two years how to spend the roughly A$300 million it is to be paid for the sale of its European milling and baking business.
Goodman chief executive David Hearn said the company was in no hurry to spend the money on an acquisition and would consider returning the funds to shareholders by way of a share buy-back.
"We are very clear we are not going to spend the money unwisely," Hearn told a business luncheon in Melbourne.
"At the point we decide there are no acquisitions worth making, we should be responsible and return the money to shareholders."
Referring to Goodman's time frame for a decision, he added: "I would say 12 to 24 months is a safe bet."
Hearn also said he expected Goodman to begin franking its dividends within two and a half years, but doubted dividends would ever be fully franked due to the nature of its business.
"We won't see franking for sure for two years," he said.
"Depending on how fast the earnings grow, we will see it somewhere between two and two and a half years."
Goodman is about a third the way through its programme of cost reductions and productivity improvements, Hearn said.
"We are still a long way away from operating at world's best practice in most of the businesses we operate in," he said.
"In general, we are a long way off the pace and therefore you can assume for the next two or three years we still have plenty to go at."

Goodman reported last Friday a 22 percent rise in net profit after abnormals to A$55.9 million for the half-year to December 31 and said it was headed for double-digit growth in annual profit for 1996/97. -- Melbourne bureau 613-9286-1421
